questions.q: Trace the growth of the national movement from the founding of the Congress to the Swadeshi Movement.

answer.text: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885, with its first session at Bombay under W.C. Bonnerjee. The early leaders, called Moderates — Dadabhai Naoroji, who put forward the drain of wealth theory, and Gopal Krishna Gokhale — relied on petitions, speeches and appeals to British justice.
By the early twentieth century, leaders like Tilak, who declared 'Swaraj is my birthright', along with Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal, demanded self-rule and bolder action.

The Partition of Bengal in 1905 by Lord Curzon provoked the Swadeshi Movement, in which people boycotted British goods and promoted Indian, or swadeshi, products, marking a more militant phase of nationalism.

questions.q: Describe the major mass movements led by Mahatma Gandhi against British rule.
answer: After returning from South Africa in 1915, Gandhi led the freedom struggle through satyagraha, or non-violent resistance.

answer.text: Launched in 1920, it called on Indians to boycott British schools, courts, titles and foreign cloth. It was withdrawn in 1922 after the violence at Chauri Chaura.
Begun in 1930 with the Dandi Salt March, in which Gandhi broke the salt law, it spread defiance of unjust laws across the country.
Launched in 1942 with the call to 'Do or Die', it demanded the immediate end of British rule.

answer: These mass movements united millions and made independence, achieved in 1947, inevitable.
